statement: On a hundred square, 1 to 10 fill the top row, 11 to 20 the next, and so on. Ana starts on 23, moves 3 squares down, then 2 squares left. Where does she land?

choices.misconception: I added 1 for each square down, as if moving down worked like moving right.
I mixed up the moves and went 2 squares down and 3 squares left.
I counted the starting row as one of the three, so I only went 2 rows down.
I moved 2 squares right instead of left.

hints: What happens to a number when you move one square down?
In a grid with rows of 10, moving down one square adds 10 and moving left one square takes away 1. Apply each move in turn, starting from 23.
Three squares down from 23 is 23 + 30 = 53. Now move 2 squares left.

solutions.reliable: Each row has 10 numbers, so one square down adds 10 and one square left takes away 1. Three squares down from 23 is 23 + 30 = 53, and two squares left is 53 - 2 = 51. Check: 51 is in the same column as 21, two columns to the left of 23. The transferable idea: in a grid with rows of n, moving down adds n and moving left takes away 1.

whyOnTest: Number grids test the link between row length and the size of a vertical step, and each distractor misreads one move.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
